why: Paper 1 (the atomic reference): a direct test of the valence rule on darbon's hydride DH5 (4D element 7), which the census settles by counting, closed-shell Hartree–Fock and three random nudges. Here: the full 24 × 24 Cartesian curvature matrix at the census geometry by central differences (eight shares), and balanced alternatives DH5 → DH4 + H and → DH3 + H2 with each fragment in its lowest spin (both tried), by UHF and UMP2.
